body.statement:
Let \(n\geq1\) and \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}<U_{\mathrm{bd}}\).  Under independent \(D_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), Hull's affine estimator
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{AF}}
 =\frac{\sqrt n}{\sqrt n+1}\widehat\tau^*,\qquad
 \widehat\tau^*=\frac2n\sum_{i=1}^n(2D_i-1)
 \left(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\frac{U_{\mathrm{bd}}+L_{\mathrm{bd}}}{2}\right),
\]
has maximum squared-error risk over all schedules in \([L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]^{2n}\) equal to
\(
 \Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2.
\)
Consequently \(\mathfrak R_n^\star[L_{\mathrm{bd}},U_{\mathrm{bd}}]\leq\Delta_{\mathrm{bd}}^2/(\sqrt n+1)^2\).

\begin{corollary}\label{corollary1}
Over all affine estimators, without imposing  \eqref{eq:equivariance}, minimax MSE is $(U-L)^2/(\sqrt{N}+1)^2$. A minimax procedure is independent random assignment with the estimator
\begin{align*}
\hat\beta^*_{AF} = \frac{\sqrt{N}}{\sqrt{N}+1}\hat\beta^*
\end{align*}
Moreover, $\kappa_N<(\sqrt{N}+1)^{-2}$ when $N>2$ such that $\hat\beta^*_{NL}$ has strictly lower worst-case MSE.
\end{corollary}

\[
\max\left\{\frac{\lambda^2}{N},(1-\lambda)^2\right\}.
\]
Minimizing this expression over $\lambda$ gives $\lambda_N=\frac{\sqrt N}{\sqrt N+1}$ and 
\[
\min_\lambda
\max\left\{\frac{\lambda^2}{N},(1-\lambda)^2\right\}
=
\frac{1}{(\sqrt N+1)^2}.
\]

This lower bound is attained with $c=0$ and $\lambda=\lambda_N$.
Indeed, for any $(k,m)$, $|q_{k,m}|\leq 1-\frac{m}{N}$, and, since $\frac{\lambda_N^2}{N}=(1-\lambda_N)^2$, equation \eqref{A1} yields
\[
R_{k,m}(0,\lambda_N)
=
\frac{1}{(\sqrt N+1)^2}
\left\{
\frac{m}{N}+q_{k,m}^2
\right\}
\leq
\frac{1}{(\sqrt N+1)^2}
\left\{
\frac{m}{N}+
\left(1-\frac{m}{N}\right)^2
\right\}
\leq
\frac{1}{(\sqrt N+1)^2}.
\]

Let
\[
d_x^A=1+\lambda_N\left(\frac{2x}{N}-1\right).
\]
The preceding calculation shows that every endpoint risk of $d^A$ is
at most $(\sqrt N+1)^{-2}$. Its Bernstein extension is
\[
B_{d^A}(Z)
=
1+\lambda_N\left(\frac2N\sum_i Z_i-1\right),
\]
since $\sum_x x p_x(Z)=\sum_iZ_i$. Thus this extension is precisely
the normalized version of $\lambda_N\widehat\beta^*$. By the
separate-convexity argument in Step 3 of the proof of Theorem 1, its
maximum risk over the full cube is attained at a vertex. Hence the affine minimax risk is
\[
\frac{(U-L)^2}{(\sqrt N+1)^2}.
\]

body.justification: Hull's closed-form affine rule supplies a simple certified independent-design upper bound at the three smaller even sizes.
body.gap: The cited result is a global bounded-class upper certificate, while the new work is the strict finite comparison obtained from exact balanced-design binary saddles.
body.consumer: The bounded-class theorem combines this upper bound with the endpoint-subclass lower bound for balanced complete randomization.
